name: bsk CLI 0.4.2
body:
BrowserSkill CLI 0.4.2 adds MCP access and more reliable updates, cancellation, and action outcomes. Use it with extension 0.4.2 for the browser-side fixes below.

### Added

- **MCP server:** `bsk mcp` exposes BrowserSkill over stdio through the existing daemon and extension. `bsk install-skill --mcp` configures Codex, Claude Code, or Cursor. The initial adapter covers its tool schemas; file transfers, recording, and full-page screenshot export remain available through the CLI or DSH plugin.
- **Controller identity:** session startup accepts an agent name, project, and color, shown in the extension's shared-control overlay and session metadata.
- **Date and time inputs:** `fill` supports `date`, `time`, `datetime-local`, `month`, and `week`, with format and min/max validation.

### Changed

- CLI and daemon updates prefer the official website's domestic download source and fall back to GitHub on download or verification failures. Archive fallback stays on the selected version and retains SHA256 verification. Explicit manifest overrides continue to use only the configured source.
- Borrowed tabs return relative to their original neighbors, with improved pinned-tab and group restoration. Eligible requests can automatically borrow a tab when borrow confirmation is disabled.
- Shared control now waits for two seconds of quiet after the person's last completed action, up from 650 ms.

### Fixed

- Timed-out page actions cancel and await bounded cleanup. Errors preserve execution phase, effect state, and operation identity. Missing receipts remain explicitly uncertain; CLI and MCP guidance asks callers to inspect the application result before choosing another action.
- Cancellation arriving before daemon RPC registration is retried within a shared two-second confirmation/response budget, reducing screenshots that keep a session busy after the caller stops.
- Windows remote pairing, credential rotation, and revocation retry authorization snapshot replacement when concurrent readers cause `Access is denied`.
- Shared-control sync recovers missing frame collectors, reports failed child frames safely, preserves human holds, and retries transient coverage failures within its deadline.
- Recovery guidance identifies the sync reply's top-level `observation_id`. Borrow guidance explains closed tabs and unavailable confirmation UI.
- DSH fill/select values beginning with `-` are passed as values instead of being parsed as CLI options.

### Coordinated extension fixes

- Restore legacy `mousewheel` handlers, including Bilibili player volume controls, even when no BrowserSkill task is active.
- Avoid repeated page reloads caused by enabling console capture before it is requested.
- Prevent truncated emoji text from invalidating an entire daemon reply and leaving commands waiting until timeout.
- Let automated clicks reach page controls beneath the shared-control toolbar; preserve successful Enter-triggered navigation receipts.
- Keep scrolling, ineffective keys, and focus alone from unnecessarily taking control; release completed/cancelled gestures and composition holds correctly.
- Preserve main-document target actions across unrelated iframe refreshes, recheck selectors after node replacement, and associate repeated action labels with their own DOM containers.
- Verify actual window and viewport sizes after resizing, and refresh shared-control observations.
- Extend sensitive-field redaction across shared-control state, expectation failures, extraction, recording, and saved HTML debug evidence; recognize compound autocomplete tokens and keep recognized password fields masked after reveal. Redact vendor credential headers in debug evidence.

### Upgrade

1. Finish active browser tasks and run `bsk update --yes`. Restart foreground or supervisor-managed daemons in their owning terminal or process manager; after replacing the executable with an installer, run `bsk daemon restart`.
2. Install [extension 0.4.2](https://github.com/Tencent/BrowserSkill/releases/tag/ext-v0.4.2) and update the DSH plugin to 0.4.2. Store review may delay availability.
3. Reload the browser-skill instructions. DSH users should restart the profile and invoke `/browser-skill` again. Restart MCP clients after adding their configuration.
4. Check `bsk --version`, `bsk status`, and `bsk doctor`.

### What's Changed

name: career-ops v1.39.0: After the Scan
body:
<!-- co:release-notes:career-ops-v1.39.0 -->
This release is about the steps after the scan: reading an interview invite, keeping your CV in your own words and checking a UK visa sponsor before you apply. It comes from 99 people over two weeks, 69 of them contributing for the first time.

## Highlights

- **Interview invites, read for you.** Paste an invite and `invite-match.mjs` lists what it asks of you (no AI, a recording, camera on, ID, a panel) (#5734) and drafts a short clarification email that you send yourself (#6100). `panelist-roles.mjs` classifies the people on the panel by role (#5799), and what an interviewer said they care about carries into your plan for the next round (#5801). All by @Schlaflied.
- **Your CV, in your words.** PDF and LaTeX output stop when generated text adds a stock resume phrase or a dash that your own CV does not use. Lines you wrote stay as they are. (#6178 by @mbrow190)
- **Less of you in the prompt.** With `privacy.redact_contact_info: true` in `config/profile.yml`, the Gemini, OpenAI and OpenRouter evaluator scripts take your name, email, phone and profile links out of the prompt (#2427 by @GambitATJ). Values you list in `config/privacy.yml` stop a request from the standalone evaluator scripts before it is sent (#5571 by @asimthaha). Both are opt-in, and neither changes what your coding agent sends.
- **A UK visa sponsor check.** `node sponsor-check.mjs --company "<name>"` looks the employer up in the Home Office register of licensed sponsors, and `--tracker` checks the employers in your tracker. It only reads. (#5790 by @foayenix)
- **Sixteen more places to look.** Apple (#5496 by @kellymmcgrath), ApplicantPro (#6252 by @Schlaflied), Bulldogjob (#6253 by @momoscape), ClearCompany, Homerun and WP Job Manager boards (#5918, #5785, #5878 by @benbalter), Darwinbox (#6416 by @okeken), Deel (#6189 by @dgitman), Factorial (#6394 by @artemtrofymenko), GermanTechJobs (#6346 by @faramirezs), jobs.cz and prace.cz (#5631 by @kosinal), Keka (#6199 by @darkpandawarrior), Notion (#5616 by @IaroslavMazur), Paylocity (#5687 by @ilyakanevskiy) and Zucchetti InRecruiting (#5984 by @Fede046).

### If you run scan from a script

- A misspelled top-level key in `portals.yml` now stops `scan.mjs` with exit code 1 and names the file, the key and the likely spelling. Before, the scan found nothing and exited 0. (#6107 by @mbrow190)
- `scan.mjs` exits 2 when none of its targets could be read. (#5720 by @vliggio)

## Updating

Run `node update-system.mjs apply --confirm` in your career-ops folder. If you said no to the update prompt earlier, this is the same command.

### Thank you

This release carries 450 pull requests from 99 people, 69 of them contributing for the first time.

## What's Changed
### Features
* perf(ego-browser): collapse click actionability checks into one injected call by @joway in https://github.com/citrolabs/ego-lite/pull/534
### Fixes
* fix(ego-browser): isolate default screenshot paths across runs in the shared Node process by @joway in https://github.com/citrolabs/ego-lite/pull/492
### Documentation
* docs: sync README benchmarks and comparison table with lite.ego.app, add a Windows download by @braxtonROSE4 in https://github.com/citrolabs/ego-lite/pull/486
### Other Changes
* fix(ego-browser): scope page ledgers by browser instance by @joway in https://github.com/citrolabs/ego-lite/pull/466
* build(ego-browser): unwrap soft-wrapped prose in the printed usage guide by @joway in https://github.com/citrolabs/ego-lite/pull/469
* refactor(skill): split into entry Skill and versioned usage guide by @joway in https://github.com/citrolabs/ego-lite/pull/449
* fix(ego-browser): report stuck requests on networkidle timeouts and stop e2e budget cascades by @joway in https://github.com/citrolabs/ego-lite/pull/473
* fix(ego-browser): remind agents to release task spaces they still control by @joway in https://github.com/citrolabs/ego-lite/pull/474
* fix(ego-browser): list and claim user spaces that were never renamed by @joway in https://github.com/citrolabs/ego-lite/pull/475
* ci: allow release branches cut from dev to target main by @joway in https://github.com/citrolabs/ego-lite/pull/477
* fix(ego-browser): resume and detach every auto-attached non-frame target by @joway in https://github.com/citrolabs/ego-lite/pull/479
* fix(ego-browser): enable Ego automation hooks on every Page session by @joway in https://github.com/citrolabs/ego-lite/pull/480
* feat(skill): render a usage guide per operating system by @joway in https://github.com/citrolabs/ego-lite/pull/481
* Revert "fix(ego-browser): remind agents to release task spaces they still control" by @joway in https://github.com/citrolabs/ego-lite/pull/489
* feat(ego-browser): flag content outside the viewport in default snapshots by @joway in https://github.com/citrolabs/ego-lite/pull/494
* fix(ego-browser): fall back when wheel input cannot bring a target into view by @joway in https://github.com/citrolabs/ego-lite/pull/497
* perf(ego-browser): drop fixed settle delays from actions and fail fast on idle pages by @joway in https://github.com/citrolabs/ego-lite/pull/510
* refactor(ego-browser): use a six-digit suffix for default screenshot names by @joway in https://github.com/citrolabs/ego-lite/pull/511
* ci: add Codex PR review workflow by @joway in https://github.com/citrolabs/ego-lite/pull/526
* fix(ego-browser): retry transient rename errors when writing page ledgers by @joway in https://github.com/citrolabs/ego-lite/pull/531
* fix(ego-browser): bound session setup waits and name an unresponsive Page by @joway in https://github.com/citrolabs/ego-lite/pull/532
* fix(ci): restore Star History updates and round Y axis bounds by @yarin-zhang in https://github.com/citrolabs/ego-lite/pull/572
* fix(ego-browser): let finish() close the blank anchor tab left by the last Page close by @joway in https://github.com/citrolabs/ego-lite/pull/575
* fix(plugins): bring agent plugin packages up to current host specs by @WUXM5 in https://github.com/citrolabs/ego-lite/pull/576
* fix(ego-browser): retry a snapshot whose capture straddles a document commit by @joway in https://github.com/citrolabs/ego-lite/pull/585
* fix(ego-browser): share one guid-named download directory across Pages and processes by @joway in https://github.com/citrolabs/ego-lite/pull/587
* fix(plugins): keep published npm packages valid without republishing by @WUXM5 in https://github.com/citrolabs/ego-lite/pull/588
* feat(plugins): publish the npm packages under the @ego-lite scope by @WUXM5 in https://github.com/citrolabs/ego-lite/pull/589
* docs(readme): replace the top banner image by @braxtonROSE4 in https://github.com/citrolabs/ego-lite/pull/596
* fix(ego-browser): write page ledgers as versioned files instead of renaming over them by @joway in https://github.com/citrolabs/ego-lite/pull/602
* docs(plugins): drop Skill precedence notes from host READMEs by @WUXM5 in https://github.com/citrolabs/ego-lite/pull/604
* fix(ego-browser): stop a navigation that has not committed by the goto timeout by @joway in https://github.com/citrolabs/ego-lite/pull/603
* feat(plugins): version the npm packages apart from the plugin by @WUXM5 in https://github.com/citrolabs/ego-lite/pull/605
* fix(ego-browser): stop a pending navigation once an unresponsive-Page wait ran out by @joway in https://github.com/citrolabs/ego-lite/pull/606
* fix(ego-browser): keep a locked page ledger version instead of replacing it by @joway in https://github.com/citrolabs/ego-lite/pull/607
* ci: allow hotfix/* and docs/* branches as PR sources into main by @qddegtya in https://github.com/citrolabs/ego-lite/pull/615

name: Context Mode 2.0
body:
# Context Mode 2.0

Context Mode is a free, local, open source plugin for 10 coding agents. The agent writes a short script, the script runs in a local sandbox, and only the answer enters the context window. The full output stays in a SQLite index on your machine, so the agent can search it later.

2.0 is a full rewrite: 9 tools, hooks on all 10 agents, one database per project, and a bench you can run yourself.

## Upgrade from 1.x

Use your agent's own command. Then restart the agent and run `/ctx-upgrade` in it: it replaces the old 1.x entries and keeps your own settings. `/ctx-doctor` then shows PASS or a fix for each check.

| Agent | Install or update |
|---|---|
| Claude Code | `claude plugin marketplace add mksglu/context-mode` then `claude plugin install context-mode@context-mode` |
| Codex | `codex plugin marketplace add mksglu/context-mode` then `codex plugin add context-mode@context-mode`, and once: `npm i -g context-mode` and `context-mode setup --agents codex` (trusts the plugin hooks) |
| Gemini CLI | `gemini extensions install https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode` (update: `gemini extensions update context-mode`) |
| Qwen Code | `qwen extensions install https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode:context-mode` (update: `qwen extensions update context-mode`) |
| Pi | `pi install npm:context-mode` (update: `pi update --extensions`) |
| OpenCode | `opencode plugin add context-mode` (update: `opencode plugin update`) |
| Copilot CLI | `npm i -g context-mode` then `context-mode setup --agents copilot-cli` |
| Kiro | `npm i -g context-mode` then `context-mode setup --agents kiro` |
| VS Code (Copilot) | `npm i -g context-mode` then `context-mode setup --agents vscode` |
| ZCode | `npm i -g context-mode` then `context-mode setup --agents zcode` |

Every block, with check and remove steps: [README, Install](https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode#install) and the [Install guide](https://contextmode.ai/docs/engine/install?utm_source=github&utm_medium=release&utm_content=2-0-0).

## Highlights

- **Thinking in Code.** The agent sends a script, and only what it prints comes back. On 5,000 JSON records (1,039,898 B) the agent got 254 B. [How it works, step 5](https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode#thinking-in-code)
- **Sandbox tools.** `ctx_execute` runs shell, JavaScript, TypeScript, Python and other runtimes in the project folder; `ctx_batch` runs many commands, indexes the output and searches it in one call. [Tools](https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode#tools)
- **99.4% of output bytes saved.** Median over the 36 bench rows with 10 KB or more of raw output, 5 runs per row. [Bench file](https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode/blob/main/bench/results/2026-11-01-darwin-arm64.md)
- **Search.** Each chunk goes into a Porter-stemmed FTS5 table and a trigram table. `ctx_search` ranks each with BM25 and joins them with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (k = 60), with a spelling fix from the indexed words. 20 queries: 1.62 ms median. [How it works, step 7](https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode#how-it-works)
- **One search for content and memory.** `ctx_search` reads the index and every agent's memory files (such as `AGENTS.md`) in one call. [How it works, step 7](https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode#how-it-works)
- **Run, then replace.** On hosts that run the tool first, output over 4,096 B goes into the index whole, and the agent gets the best chunks. One 666,796 B log put 3,380 B into the context. [Longer sessions](https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode#longer-sessions)
- **Session continuity.** The hooks keep a journal of prompts, edits, commands and errors. After compaction, `ctx_resume` brings back a state block of at most 2,048 B: a 442,893 B session came back in 2,019 B. [Long sessions guide](https://contextmode.ai/docs/engine/long-sessions?utm_source=github&utm_medium=release&utm_content=2-0-0)
- **A full session.** One scripted debugging session: 281,261 B of raw output, 3,266 B in the context. [Bench file](https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode/blob/main/bench/results/2026-11-01-darwin-arm64.md)
- **`ctx_stats` report.** Shows how much output stayed out of the context, this session and all-time. [Tools](https://contextmode.ai/docs/engine/tools?utm_source=github&utm_medium=release&utm_content=2-0-0)
- **`ctx_doctor` with issue reports.** One row per check, each with PASS or a fix command. When a check still fails, doctor writes a report file and a ready `gh issue` command for the agent to show you. [Doctor guide](https://contextmode.ai/docs/engine/doctor?utm_source=github&utm_medium=release&utm_content=2-0-0)
- **10 agents with hooks.** Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, Pi, OpenCode, Copilot CLI, Kiro, VS Code and ZCode. A hook adds 7.5 ms to 12.3 ms over a bare `node` start. [Agents guide](https://contextmode.ai/docs/engine/agents?utm_source=github&utm_medium=release&utm_content=2-0-0)
- **Node's own SQLite.** The store uses the built-in `node:sqlite`: no native module to build, no Bun. [How it works, step 10](https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode#how-it-works)
- **Windows.** CI runs setup, doctor, a hook and an MCP handshake for all 10 agents on Windows, Linux and macOS. [WINDOWS.md](https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode/blob/main/docs/architecture/release/WINDOWS.md)
- **A bench you can run.** `cd bench && node run.mjs` runs offline with plain Node and writes the same tables. [bench/README.md](https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode/blob/main/bench/README.md), [Benchmarks guide](https://contextmode.ai/docs/engine/benchmarks?utm_source=github&utm_medium=release&utm_content=2-0-0)

## Changes for 1.x users

<details><summary>What changed and how to move</summary>

- **Node 24.15.0 or later.** 1.x needed Node 22.5. 2.0 uses `node:sqlite`, and 24.15.0 is the first version with it unflagged. Bun and better-sqlite3 are gone.
- **Data store.** Each project has one `context.db` under `~/.context-mode`. 2.0 starts a new index and does not copy 1.x data. `ctx_doctor` shows where the 1.x data is and its size, and nothing gets deleted without asking you.
- **Setup.** The CLI has three commands: `context-mode setup`, `context-mode doctor` and `context-mode upgrade`. Setup shows a plan, saves your config, then applies the plan; it also replaces 1.x entries. The 1.x hook forms (`context-mode hook <platform> <event>` and `mcp`) still run, and doctor asks you to run setup to rewrite them.
- **Tools.** Nine tools: `ctx_execute`, `ctx_batch`, `ctx_index`, `ctx_search`, `ctx_resume`, `ctx_stats`, `ctx_doctor`, `ctx_upgrade`, `ctx_purge`.
  - `ctx_execute_file` is now `ctx_execute` with a `file` field.
  - `ctx_batch_execute` is now `ctx_batch`.
  - `ctx_fetch_and_index` is now `ctx_index` with a `url` field.
  - `ctx_insight` and `context-mode insight` are gone.
- **Removed in 2.0:** statusline, HTTP daemon mode, the CLI `index` and `search` commands, routing files in your project (`CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md` templates). The routing now lives in the tool descriptions, so setup never writes your instruction files.
- **Agents.** 2.0 supports 10 agents. Cursor, JetBrains Copilot, Kimi, Codex Desktop, OpenClaw, OMP (Oh My Pi), Antigravity (agy) and Zed are not in 2.0. To keep one of them, stay on 1.0.169.
- **Your settings stay.** Setup and `/ctx-upgrade` keep your own hooks, hook timeouts, `permissions.deny` and MCP entries.

**The step to move:** run your agent's command from the table above, restart the agent, run `/ctx-upgrade`, then `/ctx-doctor`. If you installed 1.x with npm, remove the old global package only after that: `npm uninstall -g context-mode` comes last, because 1.x hooks call the global command until `/ctx-upgrade` replaces them.

</details>

## Features and fixes

This part covers 307 commits since 1.0.169: 72 features, 222 fixes and 13 performance changes.

### Search

<details><summary>15 changes</summary>

- `ctx_search` ranks every agent's memory files together with indexed content, and a source filter that names a memory file searches that file. 4415e2f7 5ef0a2a6
- Search ranks in layers: stopwords, chunks that match every term first, then an OR fallback when hits are few. ba1b9b7a 60e1b62f
- Search uses porter stemming and a chunk title column. c1fd04f3
- Search adds a trigram table, RRF fusion and typo correction from the index vocabulary. f8f7850e
- Markdown chunks split on headings and keep the title path; code fences never split, and inline content with a heading or fence chunks as markdown. 697b13a1 7a26490f
- Fetched HTML turns into readable markdown before chunking. 7b47de82
- Snippets are verbatim, fence-aware and chosen by score; a snippet takes a whole neighbour fence, and typo words place it by prefix. 62ac32c2 de09a613
- A relevance reply holds 5 hits, and `More:` pages the rest with one line per cursor. c312684e c028484a
- Replies are lean when the top hit holds every query word, and smaller on small sources with no empty query blocks. c028484a 0841fda6
- A search over a JSON source returns whole BM25-ranked rows. 30c84f3a
- A source query with no matching words lists that source's chunks by position. ce89bfc4
- A stored label wins over a handle; a long label shows as handle, size and preview. a621d67d
- A NUL in a query splits words and gives a normal result. eb523586
- Chunks keep a line over the small cap whole, so search returns the whole line. 6fefd968
- Search typo correction, scoped ranking and prepared statements run faster (perf). d36b505e e52388ac 36ebb21b

</details>

### Sandbox (ctx_execute / ctx_batch)

- `ctx_execute` gives a bare reply with the whole output on exit 0, and a 4 KB preview when output is stored. 06535f10
- `ctx_batch` replies show the exit code only when it is not zero and a pointer only when output was left out. d4c98b3c
- Each `ctx_batch` call answers from its own sources first, under its own label `ctx_batch:<turn>:<n>`. 5dd8a04d
- The `mvn.cmd` rewrite from #782 is back. 4fe21f7d
- Every tool description starts with an exact example call; a bad call gets one line with the correct call on all hosts. b66edb3c
- Server instructions and the `ctx_execute` description are shorter, so each session starts with fewer tokens (perf). c70f1e20

### Hooks and routing

<details><summary>16 changes</summary>

- The hook never errors: all 10 hosts share one fallback decision. 6de98259
- The shell-dump deny checks every command in a chain, follows `cd` and unwraps `zsh -c`. 9fba2c52
- The policy scans command substitutions inside `$(( ))`. 8e7edda9
- Unbounded PowerShell file dumps (`Get-Content`, `gc`, `type`, `[IO.File]::ReadAllText`) get the same deny as `cat`. 765be33d
- The Windows deny glob uses forward slashes and a drive-less `//` anchor. 872216b8
- The Read deny is one line with the exact `ctx_execute` call for the file. 6c9f8a37
- The main agent runs the tool, then the hook replaces large output with the best chunks. 3f4a4d0b 16df63bd
- The replace ranks chunks by the call's intent or the last user prompt words; with no description, intent comes from the command, path, pattern or URL. 8db7170f ae0a3169
- The replace shapes output by content type, reads the whole stored Bash output, and the digest header carries counts only. 85c34f06 41eb547a ed0108c3
- Non-ctx MCP results and Grep content results get the same replace; one-off categorical rows count as rare units. 90e3dce9 37cc74b0
- JSON output gets a digest header with the schema and numeric extremes for a named key, inside its own 256 B budget. 94332734 2ebdf842
- The replacement names the stored source by short id, size and the search call to run. 4bf03c9c c98b71a6 cccb08ca 5e4a9737 d5c1302c
- The handle line adds the prompt words the output holds as a second query. 7e4d3975
- Replace output stays clean at an empty body and the selection budget stops at 0. 0a4a77de fef78434
- Hook texts name tools with each host's own tool prefix on all 10 hosts. 054eb84e
- The hook reads stdin as a stream in its entry. 693403b2

</details>

### Memory and session continuity

- The anchored state block has a decisions section. f249ef09
- Recall runs at the turn boundary after compaction. 0f1ea796
- Ledger line units build at PostToolUse and feed one ranked recall query. 83e0e8be
- `ctx_resume` lists sources by short id and goal line units. 81be2830
- The MCP server uses the host session id from `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`. 55990426

### Stats

- `ctx_stats` gives a detailed text report with a short tool description. 8ebc8d4b 4ca12eac
- The report shows context window share, hook work, largest outputs, last 7 days cards and stacked bars. 859495bf
- Rows add up, headings are scoped, blocks do not repeat, and the footer carries UTM links. 77cae47c
- One `ctx_stats` reply reads one database snapshot. d56aaf82
- The journal records returned bytes as the bytes the model got, after the replace decision, in the main agent and subagents. ec5c3739 e18a93c3
- In-process `ctx_*` calls on OpenCode and Pi write the server's journal row. 80e687dd

### Doctor

<details><summary>15 changes</summary>

- `ctx_doctor` shows an environment line, docs links and a ready agent issue report; `.github/AGENT_ISSUE.md` is in the repo. 2f807ae0 baaa3149
- The report names the exact context-mode command to run. e37a9619 4471e083
- The report fits 80 columns, with one docs link under the table and a wrapped `gh` command. 88972ba2
- `ctx_doctor` heals an orphan WAL and always returns its report; the report is stored whole and long echoes are named by id. 14e488eb 42750b15
- The version check starts git directly, names the exact cause, and compares in the bundle's channel: npm dist-tag first, git tags as fallback. 1eaec71e a65cd5ad b542a679
- New checks: hook registered, hook runs, hook seen and skills. 780424cc
- The hook-runs check confirms the saving effect on each host. 2e1fe507
- Doctor and setup fail when a host would run none of the installed hooks: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, Pi, OpenCode, Copilot CLI, Kiro, VS Code and ZCode. 22501180 a66617dc 6cd19e83 56f72846 6cba095b 2600dbf7 238e9c32 da5120dd 807ae9a5 5ef1f189
- The hook cost check covers all 10 agents, measures over bare node and runs 3 to 9 pairs, more only while over the bound. b542a679 7b68b5b8 37a48049
- The hook cost check uses recorded native payloads and labels old hook errors as past. ea4179fd
- The config check matches setup for Codex and MCP hosts and names setup for a missing MCP entry. 9dd44149 b542a679
- The config check accepts the quoted absolute-path hook command that setup writes. 3d8c4914
- Report-only 1.x findings do not fail an agent that is set up. 9bce0b50
- Doctor verifies a native Codex plugin install and native Gemini CLI and Qwen Code extension installs; a disabled extension names the enable command. 9781e1c9 518f4065
- The report path prints with forward slashes on Windows. 6598e099

</details>

### Setup and install

<details><summary>12 changes</summary>

- New `setup`, `doctor` and `upgrade` commands with prompts, a report, typo hints, progress and rollback on abort. 966af39f b1d4f91b 0483b1cb ef8c7274
- Each command has its own `--help`; `help <command>` opens it, and output falls back to 80 columns when a terminal reports 0. 02cb17a6 d3638ec4
- `setup --print <agent>` prints the manual step for that agent and writes nothing. 68e87b8e
- Setup writes the hook and skill channel for every agent. a90f47d5 c3eb44c7
- Install docs lead with each agent's native install command, then the update, check and next steps, in short plain commands. 2e64a6b2 3c0656a2
- CLI help, setup and doctor output use 2.0 wording. 4b1a7629
- `--yes` works with no terminal. e86bddcd
- Agent CLI install steps get 120 s, so a first run can unpack its package. feb8de11
- The hook gate takes the best of 3 rounds, so host noise does not roll back a good install. 0c9613ae
- Setup finds its own hook entries by `hook.mjs --agent <id>` and rewrites 1.x hook commands in flat hook files. b9b1a58e 87a44c97
- Home-dir skills render from the bare-name skill dir with no doubled tool prefix. a7e38076
- The CLI, server and hook run on Node 22 and on Node below 22.3; setup reaches its report even on an EPIPE. 257a5190 7b0df434 80fabdb4 249f03bf

</details>

### Per agent

<details><summary>50 changes</summary>

**Claude Code**

- The PowerShell tool routes like Bash in PreToolUse, PostToolUse and hook matchers (#1212). f65e5313
- Setup enables a disabled plugin; doctor fails on `disableAllHooks`. 22501180
- Setup, doctor and plugin root honour `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. 01e06543
- The project comes from `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, then payload cwd, then `process.cwd()`. 71ae2bcf
- The decoder names missing required fields and defaults the rest. 78de5abf
- Doctor fails on a stale plugin copy; setup and upgrade run `claude plugin update` and keep the dist-tag. 1aa584de
- Setup and doctor find the real `claude` past a PATH shim and print the binary used. 37fd45c8
- Doctor judges the install this project uses (scope, projectPath, enabledPlugins, `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`) and reads the plugin root from `installed_plugins.json`. b353268f 4653f730
- Claude Code gets its own rendered skills dir. 02e28bc4
- The npm package carries `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` with the owner object. 1d0c754b 5c41eb61
- Uninstall deletes a marketplace root only inside the plugin cache. 58d6b744
- Claude Code never runs the Gemini hooks file under `/bin/sh`. 96e3672b

**Codex**

- Setup trusts its own plugin hooks after a native install and after `hooks/list`; doctor fails on untrusted hooks with one shared check. a66617dc 95080050 b93adcef
- The trust key handles Codex 0.166 composite hashes, an empty app-server reply, a symlinked HOME and the `codexHome` spelling Codex reports. bbd7cefd 4fb62aa6 2f3bc32b
- Setup waits up to 5 s for Codex to close after `hooks/list` and ends the whole process tree. 7c726850 16a4bcc5
- Config, hooks, skills and doctor follow `CODEX_HOME` and the home the running plugin sits in. 952e2fc2 da6f91ea 9e08df05
- The native plugin MCP resolves the host workspace, not the plugin cache dir. c988ff43
- The MCP entry sets `omit_tools_from = ["deferred"]` and `default_tools_approval_mode = approve`, so ctx tools are direct. 056ef921 efdedf4c
- Setup reads and edits any valid TOML 1.0 config. bf511986
- On Windows the hook command starts with bare node, since Codex 0.166 runs hooks in PowerShell. 135120eb 31bb89dc
- Plugin skills use Codex tool names; the marketplace on main points at the built plugin. d6f964fe c961fdaa

**Gemini CLI**

- The row lists native tool ids, so shell and read rules reach BeforeTool. ecbe91f7
- BeforeTool denies a one-file shell dump over the cap before it runs. 5aaf4562
- A resume hint shows on the first BeforeAgent of a session. 831368b1
- The extension carries the `extensionPath` server path and `hooks/hooks.json`; setup links it and never waits on stdin. 8d11ff6b 8b6e4b66
- Skills render with Gemini tool names; doctor reads the extension hook file with the `${/}` separator. 46a58920 8a369307
- Setup accepts the Windows exit-time crash of `gemini extensions link` when the extension is listed. c3039618

**Qwen Code**

- The extension carries the `extensionPath` server path and hooks key; docs show the native extension install. 8feb0c45 c507e005
- The skills channel is the package `skills/` dir with Qwen tool names. b20637f0

**Pi**

- Pi gets the same system prompt every turn, so the prompt cache holds. e1b98217
- The out tree has a Pi-only `package.json`; skills use Pi tool names. ffd762d2 46a58920
- An empty `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` counts as unset. f98750f4

**OpenCode**

- The OpenCode 2 native install is `opencode plugin add context-mode@next`. 591197c6
- The plugin loads on OpenCode 2 and on the 1.19.4 loader. 2600c92b 78af6bec ad0e8a2f 861d607b
- One working plugin entry; doctor fails on a double or stale entry. 2600dbf7
- The bash tool routes through the hook. 2e1fe507
- Setup lists with `--pure`, follows `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, and reads `opencode.json` as JSONC. 09465cc8 7ce8d4dc 14710eb5

**Copilot CLI**

- The decoder reads the documented payload with no `hookEventName`. ff999dd4
- The own MCP tool prefix is `context-mode-`; skills and deny texts name the real tool, and shared skills serve both Copilot CLI and VS Code. dcc576e5 850821bf b195b992
- Setup checks hooks are enabled and cleans `disabledHooks`. 238e9c32
- Hooks, skills and detection follow `COPILOT_HOME`. 5094c639
- Hook entries get an explicit `powershell` field, also on VS Code. 7aaaf89e

**Kiro**

- The decoder reads camelCase tool events and the UserPromptSubmit trigger; shell matcher names follow Kiro docs. 397cc04b c507e005 18301355
- Kiro registers the shell tool `execute_bash` next to `@mcp`; deny text goes to stderr with exit 2. d13980ce
- Hooks, MCP entry, skills and detection follow `KIRO_HOME`. 663aa666

**VS Code**

- The decoder reads the camelCase hook payload and maps every documented terminal, read and fetch tool. 16fa82b0 a531951a
- The project comes from `--workspace-folder ${workspaceFolder}` and the payload cwd; `run_in_terminal` is the shell. 51fd1891
- The MCP entry goes to the user-profile `mcp.json`; doctor reads the user hook file setup writes. 38c191ee db09aee6
- Skills move to `~/.agents/skills`. b195b992

**ZCode**

- Setup writes matcher groups and `mcp.servers`/`features.mcp`; uninstall drops the nested entry. 6be8e768

</details>

### Windows

<details><summary>13 changes</summary>

- Home is `USERPROFILE` first on Windows and `HOME` first elsewhere, from one helper; doctor names `USERPROFILE` when no home is found. 7b54a2ed d6a0648d 8c9d87ad
- File writes retry a busy rename (EPERM, EBUSY, EACCES), name the held file and clean their tmp file. d7886972 31c21f76 567970c2 3874f2cf 49db0498 ee95ebb9
- Setup finds agent CLIs via PATHEXT and runs `.cmd` shims through `cmd.exe` with `/v:off`. 6fcc3112 76029ea7 37db76fe
- The shim line refuses only a `%NAME%` that `cmd.exe` would expand, so file URLs with `%7E` or `%20` pass. 2c1b1667 c38d4a2c
- Double quotes in PATH entries are cut. 0ba37287 cf1abd1b
- Every child process starts hidden. bb4045e8
- Host config files with a BOM and CRLF read correctly and keep their layout and line ends on write. cf6a3439 b3a3256d
- The sandbox shell is Git Bash from the installed Git. 46cb4ca7
- The `current` upgrade link is a junction on Windows. 941ea210
- Kiro, Copilot CLI, VS Code and Codex fixes for Windows homes and paths are in Per agent. 663aa666 5094c639 38c191ee 135120eb
- Store labels for path sources use forward slashes on every OS. bbee5c28
- Doctor prints the report path with forward slashes. 6598e099
- Hook start loads `node:fs` through `getBuiltinModule`, cutting Windows hook overhead (perf). 12a51f7c

</details>

### Store

- `closeDb` checkpoints in PASSIVE mode and skips the checkpoint on a read-only handle, so `ctx_stats` and `ctx_search` stay fast. 45145b88 086bde8b
- Writable connections run `synchronous=NORMAL`, so a COMMIT needs no fsync (perf). fbb923d9
- A reserved source row goes away when its write fails; the retention cap counts real bytes. e2a822a6 c56e86a9
- A project dir outside any git repo is a project keyed by its realpath. d32aa0cf
- `rankTexts` runs on a one-column contentless FTS5 table with the same BM25 scores (perf). 82655e34

### Performance

- The hook bundle is minified: 155 KB to 91 KB parse per call. 92f165e7
- Hook start skips `fs/promises`, readline, streams and `node:crypto`, and loads `child_process` and `randomUUID` only when needed. b227991d 4bbccb42 639da517
- The hook reads stdin and writes stdout with sync fd I/O. 6d56a48c 43d1e806
- `resolveProject` computes the project key, dir and db path on first read. 7d75314c
- PostToolUse chunks output once and selects in memory for both sizes. dd2be182
- See also the perf lines in Search, Sandbox, Windows and Store.

### Build and release

<details><summary>12 changes</summary>

- Releases run from main in one click: plan, npm publish, release commit and tag in one push, and a GitHub release; rollback is a forward commit. 4aab9952 b3db26cc 2d6ab773
- The main tree holds `plugins/claude-code`, both marketplaces and root Gemini CLI and Qwen Code manifests from the packed package. a3642a39 ace68cec c961fdaa
- Smoke tests cover the main layout, a Qwen Code leg and the native Codex commands. ebd0a746 c961fdaa
- A pushed release tag sets the version, prerelease versions build, and a prerelease GitHub release is not marked latest. 21d8e438 e2bee539 7894f2d3 630a61c6 7d377219
- The GitHub release runs after npm publish. 6136a9c0 c3a1ae26
- One config file lists the npm names a release publishes. 3f78ebd0
- The package carries `repository.url` for npm provenance. 496670bf
- The npm package ships `README.md` and `LICENSE` with absolute links, and a `cli.mjs` bin. 84f719fa 68e0af5a 207ba634
- Plugin manifests carry the 2.0 version and description; `package.json` is the source of release fields with no unused deps. 322aadc2 1e2f68fa
- Codex plugin manifests and the OpenCode package main ship in the npm package. 861d607b
- The generated tool file is rewritten only when changed, through temp and rename. adc44203
- The README shows an agent table, daily npm download charts, a working star chart and daily adoption history from GitHub and npm. fef7750a d0aee2d8 33775e3e 45caf2e6 e19d949b a74baadb 9f20042a

</details>
